title.value: Timeliness of reporting of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence results and their utility for infectious disease surveillance
title.justification: The main focus of the paper is on evaluating the timeliness and utility of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence reporting for surveillance purposes during the COVID-19 pandemic.
title.quote: Timeliness of reporting of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence results and their utility for infectious disease surveillance

extractions.description: This paper examines the timeliness of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence study reporting across various publication venues and its implications for public health surveillance and response. It evaluates the relationships between reporting speed, data quality, and representativeness in seroprevalence studies conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is the timeliness and utility of COVID-19 seroprevalence reporting for infectious disease surveillance, which is more aligned with public health rather than Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We aimed to determine the timeliness of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence studies in providing information useful for public health surveillance and further analysis.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily addresses public health surveillance, focusing on the COVID-19 pandemic, which does not fall under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: Seroprevalence studies in peer-reviewed articles and preprints are published slowly, highlighting the limita­ tions of using the academic literature to report seroprevalence during a health crisis.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper's focus on SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and public health does not align with secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
secondary_categories.quote: Seroprevalence studies estimate the prevalence of antibodies and are crucial sources of this information. Estimates of seroprevalence can inform scenario modeling, public health planning, and national policies.

primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper does not relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, it lacks a relevant sub-category in that context.
primary_sub_category.quote: Inclusion criteria, screening, data extraction and quality assessment of seroprevalence studies have also been previously described in detail

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's focus on infectious disease surveillance does not intersect with Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Timely information about population immunity can be critical for effective public health decision-making, as emphasized throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the need to improve the timeliness and robustness of seroprevalence data reporting for better public health surveillance.
applications.quote: More timely reporting of seroprevalence estimates can improve their usefulness for surveillance, enabling more effective responses during health emergencies.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence reporting and its implications for surveillance, warranting a category centered on infectious disease surveillance.
new_primary_category.quote: Seroprevalence studies in peer-reviewed articles and preprints are published slowly, highlighting the limita­ tions of using the academic literature to report seroprevalence during a health crisis.
